title: Negation with kein / nicht
summary: Negating nouns and simple statements in everyday contexts.
whyItMatters: Negation lets you say what you do not have, what something is not, and what does not happen. The key beginner distinction is whether you are negating a noun with 'kein' or negating an action, property, or larger statement with 'nicht'.

mentalModel.title: Kein belongs to the noun family
mentalModel.content: Use 'kein' where a positive sentence could use 'ein/eine' or no article: 'Ich habe einen Drucker' becomes 'Ich habe keinen Drucker.'

mentalModel.title: Nicht switches off an action or property
mentalModel.content: Use 'nicht' to negate a verb, adjective, adverb, or a more complete idea: 'Der Drucker funktioniert nicht' and 'Das Handy ist nicht neu.'

mentalModel.title: Ask what exactly is negative
mentalModel.content: If the missing thing is a noun, choose 'kein'. If the action or description is false, choose 'nicht'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use kein to negate an indefinite noun
ruleBlocks.content: Use forms of 'kein' before a noun when the positive idea would use 'ein/eine' or no article: 'Ich habe kein Handy.'

ruleBlocks.title: Match kein to gender, number, and case
ruleBlocks.content: At this stage, learn common forms as chunks: kein Computer, keine Tastatur, kein Handy, keine Computer, and accusative 'keinen Computer'.

ruleBlocks.title: Use nicht for an action or statement
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'nicht' when the verb or whole statement is negative: 'Ich arbeite heute nicht.'

ruleBlocks.title: Use nicht before a property
ruleBlocks.content: Place 'nicht' before an adjective or similar description: 'Der Computer ist nicht neu.'

sentenceStructure: 'Kein' appears directly before the noun it negates.
'Nicht' often appears near the end when it negates the general action.
'Nicht' appears before an adjective or property being negated.
The exact placement of 'nicht' becomes more detailed later; first identify what the sentence denies.

concepts: choose kein for nouns and nicht for actions or properties
use common kein forms in simple sentences
use kein across additional cases and possessive-like patterns
use contrastive negation in longer clauses

comparisons.summary: The office lesson supplies concrete noun and device contexts for saying what is unavailable or not working.
Clarification phrases often use 'nicht' in chunks such as 'Ich verstehe nicht' or 'Ich weiß nicht'.

examples.en: I do not have a printer.
The mobile phone is not new.

commonMistakes.reason: Use 'kein' to negate an indefinite noun.
A masculine direct object uses the accusative form 'keinen'.
A noun used without a definite article is normally negated with 'kein'.

specialCases: A noun with a definite article is normally negated with 'nicht': 'Das ist nicht der Drucker.'
'Kein' follows article-like endings and therefore changes with gender, number, and case.
The position of 'nicht' changes depending on what is contrasted or negated; this lesson covers the most reliable beginner patterns.
tips: Convert positive noun sentences from ein/eine to kein/keine.
Underline the exact word or idea being denied before choosing the negation.
Practice paired sentences: 'Ich habe einen Drucker' / 'Ich habe keinen Drucker'.

memoryHooks.title: Kein wears an article ending
memoryHooks.content: If the negative word stands directly with a noun like an article, think 'kein'.

memoryHooks.title: Nicht switches off the action or quality
memoryHooks.content: Use 'nicht' when the action does not happen or the description is not true.
